caption:
In 1950 two cities on Earth held more than 10 million people. In 2015 there were 29.

Watch the curve of city dwellers swell and lean right: 419 million people living in cities above 300,000 in 1950, 2.3 billion in 2015.

📊 See where big-city dwellers live, sorted by the size of their city, from 1950 to 2015 in this animated distribution. Explore how the world's urban population shifted out of mid-sized cities and into ever larger agglomerations.

Source: UN DESA Population Division, World Urbanization Prospects 2018, file F12. The panel is the 1,860 agglomerations that had reached 300,000 inhabitants by 2018, tracked backwards; 305 of them were above 300,000 in 1950, and 1,772 in 2015.
